tracks.label: Theorem proving
tracks.description: Complete a research-level theorem in Lean 4 from the main statement, without a supplied proof outline.

tracks.label: Solver engineering
tracks.description: Build a reusable program that solves unseen instances under fixed resource limits.

tracks.label: Constructions
tracks.description: Produce explicit mathematical objects or bounds with formally verified properties.

tracks.label: Open conjectures
tracks.description: Attempt a complete proof or refutation of a long-standing open research conjecture.

tasks.title: Quasipolynomial corners bounds
tasks.summary: Prove the stated quantitative bound for subsets of a finite abelian group squared that contain no nontrivial corner.
tasks.note: The full parameter conditions and quantitative bound are fixed by the task statement.

tasks.title: Discrete bidding games
tasks.summary: Prove that a player meeting the budget threshold has a legal strategy that keeps energy nonnegative in an integer-weighted directed graph.
tasks.note: Determinacy of the associated reachability bidding game is a supplied assumption.

tasks.title: Folded Reed–Solomon list decoding
tasks.summary: Prove the prescribed list-decoding bound: every Hamming ball at the stated radius contains at most the allowed number of codewords.
tasks.note: The target is the folded Reed–Solomon theorem; the task fixes all parameter assumptions.

tasks.title: Subtraction in arithmetic formulas
tasks.summary: Prove that certain graph polynomials admit small arithmetic formulas using subtraction while every monotone arithmetic formula requires exponential size.
tasks.note: The task supplies a random-matching assumption. This concerns arithmetic formulas and monotonicity.

tasks.title: Pseudorandomness of Forrelation
tasks.summary: Prove pseudorandomness of the Forrelation distribution against the specified Boolean functions, with a bound controlled by second-order Fourier coefficients.
tasks.note: Two external Gaussian-distribution results are supplied as assumptions.

tasks.title: One-dimensional bin packing
tasks.summary: Write a reusable solver that packs weighted items into equal-capacity bins while minimizing the number of bins.
tasks.note: The 39 final instances share one 1,170-second time pool. The pool must remain intact.

tasks.title: Curriculum-based timetabling
tasks.summary: Assign courses to rooms and time slots. Satisfy all hard constraints, then minimize the prescribed soft-constraint penalties.
tasks.note: Six final instances; 240 seconds of solving time per instance.

tasks.title: Weighted maximum cut
tasks.summary: Partition a weighted graph into two sets to maximize the total weight of edges crossing the partition. The checker recomputes the objective.
tasks.note: 45 final instances; 600 seconds of solving time per instance.

tasks.title: Machine reassignment
tasks.summary: Reassign processes to machines while satisfying capacity, service-conflict, location, and dependency constraints; minimize weighted load, balance, and migration costs.
tasks.note: Ten final instances; 300 seconds of solving time per instance.

tasks.title: Quantified Boolean formulas
tasks.summary: Decide whether a quantified Boolean formula is true and supply a checkable Q-resolution proof certificate as required by the task.
tasks.note: 57 final instances; 900 seconds per instance. Certificate conversion and checking have separate limits.

tasks.title: Binary codes: A(24, 10)
tasks.summary: Construct a large set of 24-bit words with pairwise Hamming distance at least 10 and formally verify it, or prove an upper bound on the maximum set size.
tasks.note: The exact submission interfaces and fixed reference values are part of the task release.

tasks.title: Graphs without triangles or 4-cycles
tasks.summary: Construct a graph on 124 vertices with as many edges as possible, and verify its vertex set, edge count, and absence of triangles and 4-cycles.
tasks.note: This Lite Lean task fixes 124 vertices; other graph sizes do not satisfy the main interface.

tasks.title: Kissing configurations in 13 dimensions
tasks.summary: Construct a large set of points on the unit sphere in thirteen-dimensional space with pairwise angles of at least 60 degrees.
tasks.note: The task uses exact certificates for distances and separation.

tasks.title: Ramsey constructions: R(4, 6)
tasks.summary: Color the edges of a complete graph red and blue, avoiding a red 4-clique and a blue 6-clique, to establish a lower bound. The task also accepts upper-bound proofs.
tasks.note: The task-specific milestone scoring rule is preserved; construction scores use their original scale.

tasks.title: Metric traveling-salesperson integrality gap
tasks.summary: Give a metric instance, a feasible solution to the subtour linear program, and a certificate bounding the shortest tour from below, to prove a large integrality gap.
tasks.note: The displayed ratio describes the research objective. The checker uses the task-specific certified bound and score.

tasks.title: The log-rank conjecture
tasks.summary: Prove or refute that deterministic two-party communication complexity is bounded by a fixed power of the logarithm of the real rank of the communication matrix.
tasks.note: A complete proof or refutation is required. Intermediate bounds receive no partial credit.

tasks.title: Evasiveness of graph properties
tasks.summary: Prove or refute that every nontrivial monotone graph property invariant under vertex relabeling requires querying every possible edge in the worst case.
tasks.note: All hypotheses in the formal statement must be retained.

tasks.title: Frege is not polynomially bounded
tasks.summary: Prove or refute the existence of a family of propositional tautologies whose shortest proofs in the fixed Frege system exceed every polynomial bound.
tasks.note: The formula language, axiom schemes, and proof system are fixed by the task.

tasks.title: Online matching in random arrival order
tasks.summary: Prove or refute the existence of a randomized online bipartite matching algorithm attaining a 3/4 competitive ratio for all sufficiently large sizes in random arrival order.
tasks.note: The sufficiently-large-size quantifier is part of the goal; a finite-size result alone is insufficient.

tasks.title: Pseudorandom generators for width-4 programs
tasks.summary: Prove or refute an efficiently computable pseudorandom generator with seed length below the logarithm-squared scale that fools length-n, width-4, read-once oblivious branching programs at error 1/n.
tasks.note: Polynomial-time computability, width 4, and the stated error are all required.
